exposure: duration of the second stage of labor (3-4 hours vs. >4 hours)
cohort: The study included 2,798 term, singleton deliveries of nulliparous patients with epidural analgesia and a second stage duration greater than 3 hours, who delivered between 2014 and 2021.
finding: While most nulliparous patients with epidural achieve vaginal delivery even after a second stage duration of > 4 hours, it is associated with increased risks of neonatal birth trauma and failed vacuum extraction.
mod_finding: A second stage duration of > 4 hours was associated with lower rates of vaginal deliveries and higher rates of vacuum extractions and cesarean deliveries compared to a 3-4 hour duration.
